A spring of spring constant 30 N m⁻¹ is suspended vertically from its top. The spring obeys
Hooke’s law. Initially the spring is not compressed and not stretched. A mass of 0.50 kg is
attached to the bottom of the spring. The mass is released from rest and falls.
Frictional effects are negligible.
In the motion that follows, what is the maximum extension of the spring?
What is the definition of power?

A model car travels at a constant velocity of 12 m s⁻¹ in a straight horizontal line. The input power
to the engine of the car is 800 W. The efficiency of the engine is 60%.
What is the total horizontal resistive force on the car?
Which statement represents the principle of conservation of energy?

options.A: Energy cannot be used faster than it is created.
options.B: The supply of energy is limited, so energy must be conserved.
options.C: The total energy in a closed system is constant.
options.D: The total energy input to a system is equal to the useful energy output.

stem:
A stone of mass 0.30 kg is thrown vertically downwards with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹ from a height of
12 m above the ground. It falls vertically until it hits the ground. Air resistance is negligible.
What is the kinetic energy of the stone just before it hits the ground?

Leonardo da Vinci proposed a flying machine that would work like a screw to lift the pilot into the
air. The ‘screw’ is rotated by the pilot.
The machine and the pilot together have a total mass of 120 kg.
Which useful output power must the pilot provide to move vertically upwards at a constant speed
of 2.5 m s⁻¹?

The work done against the frictional force in moving the box from Y to Z is 200 J.
An identical box Q is pushed in a straight line from X to Z.

How much extra work is done against the frictional force in moving P than Q?

A ball of mass 1.2 kg travels horizontally at a speed of 3.0 m s⁻¹.
The ball hits a cushion and comes to rest over a horizontal distance of 0.020 m.
What is the work done by the cushion on the ball to bring the ball to rest?
Which expression gives the efficiency of a system?

options.A: output energy useful input energy total
options.B: input energy total output energy wasted + output energy useful
options.C: input energy total output energy useful
options.D: input energy total output energy wasted

stem:
A sailboat is pushed by the wind at a constant velocity v across a lake.
The force of the wind and the velocity of the sailboat are in the same direction.
Which additional information is required to determine the work done per unit time by the wind
acting on the sailboat?

options.A: the force exerted by the wind
options.B: the distance travelled by the sailboat per unit time
options.C: the total energy input to the sailboat by the wind

A single value of the change in height Δh is used to calculate the change in gravitational potential
energy of the ball from X to Y.
What is the magnitude of Δh?
